title: Family
cando: talk about the people in my family
say what my family members do and what they are like
ask and answer questions about someone’s family
warmup: How many people are there in your family?
phrases: There are … of us in my family.
There are five of us in my family.
I’ve got one brother and two sisters.
Bitta akam (ukam) va ikkita opam (singlim) bor.
My dad works as a driver.
I get on well with my …
I get on well with my sister.
We sometimes argue, but we’re good friends.
We spend time together at the weekend.
Dam olish kunlari birga vaqt o‘tkazamiz.
How many brothers and sisters have you got?

dialogue.title: Meet Laylo’s family
dialogue.setting: Laylo is talking to Tom, a new teacher at her language centre.
lines: So, Laylo, tell me about your family. Is it big?
Quite big! There are six of us: my parents, my two brothers, my grandma and me.
No, I’m the youngest. My brothers are both older than me.
Bekzod works as a doctor, and Jasur is still a student. He studies IT.
My dad’s a driver and my mum’s a teacher. My grandma’s retired – she lives with us.
Everyone says I look like my mum. I’m closest to her, too. What about you, Tom?
Oh, I’m an only child. But I get on really well with my cousins.
That’s nice. Do you see them often?
Every weekend. We usually play football together.

pron.title: The “th” sound /ð/
pron.tip: Put the tip of your tongue between your teeth and use your voice. It is not “d” and not “z”.
pron.tip_uz: Til uchini tishlar orasiga qo‘ying va ovoz bilan ayting. Bu “d” ham, “z” ham emas.
pron.sentence: My mother and father live together with my brother.

drill.title: Make the questions — fast!
items: How many brothers and sisters have you got?
When do you spend time together?

infogap.title: Rustam’s family
infogap.intro: You and your partner have different information about Rustam’s family. Ask questions to complete your table. Don’t show your page!
infogap.intro_uz: Sizda va sherigingizda turli ma’lumotlar bor. Savol berib jadvalni to‘ldiring. Sahifangizni ko‘rsatmang!

common.title: Find three things in common
common.intro: Interview your partner. Find three things that are the same in your families.
questions: How many people are there in your family?
What do you do together at the weekend?

prompts: Who are you closest to? Why?
fluency.model: There are five of us in my family: my parents, my two younger sisters and me. I’m the oldest. My dad works as an engineer, and my mum is a teacher at a primary school. My sisters are still at school. Everyone says I look like my dad – we’re both tall and quiet. I get on well with my sisters, but sometimes we argue about the TV! I’m closest to my mum because she always listens to me. At the weekend we usually visit my grandparents and have lunch together. I really love my family.

checks: I spoke for one minute without long stops.
I used five or more key phrases.
I said “th” in mother / brother correctly.
I asked my partner at least three questions.
